title: Astrid and the Vow
premise: Cellist Freya Nakamura, whose career collapsed after a catastrophic final performance, returns home for her grandmother's eightieth birthday reunion, where her family's expectations threaten to bury her. She persuades Elias Voss, a widowed luthier repairing her shattered cello, to pose as her boyfriend for the weekend. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens into real love, but Elias is hiding that he was the stagehand responsible for the rigging failure that ended her performing life. When the truth surfaces at the reunion's final dinner, Freya must choose between the loyalty she promised him and the truth she owes herself; she forgives him not by forgetting, but by playing again — on the instrument he rebuilt — choosing a future built on honesty over the safety of silence.
about_author: A. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent a decade backstage before turning to fiction. Reyes writes romances about people rebuilding themselves out of broken instruments, old promises, and second chances.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Eight months after walking off a collapsed stage mid-concerto, Freya teaches beginner cello and avoids every invitation home. When her mother calls about Grandma Ingrid's eightieth-birthday reunion, Freya lies that she's seeing someone. The beat: grief disguised as independence.

chapters.title: A Man Who Fixes Broken Things
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She takes her cracked cello to Elias Voss's workshop, drawn to his careful hands and quiet steadiness. When he mentions he dreads eating alone at his late wife's favorite restaurant, an idea forms: he attends her reunion as her boyfriend. The beat: cautious hope sparked by mutual damage.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over coffee, they negotiate rules: no real feelings, no questions about the past, one weekend only. Both are hiding something — Freya the full story of her collapse, Elias a flinch whenever stages are mentioned. The beat: complicity that already feels like intimacy.

chapters.title: Arrival at Nakamura House
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He meets the loud, loving, suffocating Nakamura clan and discovers how much of himself he'd locked away since his wife died. Grandma Ingrid sees through the act immediately but says nothing. The beat: belonging sneaking past his defenses.

chapters.title: Duet in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Escaping the reunion's comparisons to her prodigy cousin, Freya finds Elias helping Ingrid with dumplings. Late that night, they play music together — he hums, she improvises — and the fake relationship stops feeling fake. The beat: joy she thought was gone forever.

chapters.title: What the Stagehand Saw
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback reveals the truth: Elias was working rigging the night of Freya's concert; the cable he flagged as suspect was overruled, and he's carried the guilt since. A cousin recognizes his name from the incident report. The beat: dread tightening around something precious.

chapters.title: Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Freya tells Elias about her panic attacks and shame; he nearly confesses but can't. They share a first real kiss, and both privately break their own rules. Meanwhile Ingrid quietly asks Elias what he isn't telling her granddaughter. The beat: love outrunning the lie.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the farewell dinner, the cousin confronts Elias publicly, and he confesses everything — the rigging, the warning ignored, the years of guilt. Freya flees. The beat: betrayal detonating inside tenderness.

chapters.title: Ingrid's Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Grandma Ingrid tells Freya that loyalty without truth is just hiding, and that forgiveness is a choice made daily, not a feeling granted once. Elias, packing to leave forever, receives the repaired cello — delivered with a note in Ingrid's hand. The beat: wisdom reframing heartbreak.

chapters.title: Second Chances Have Good Timing After All
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At a small benefit concert, Freya performs publicly for the first time since the collapse, on the cello Elias rebuilt, dedicating the piece to 'the man who fixed more than the instrument.' She finds him afterward and offers the whole heart, not pieces. The beat: love chosen freely over duty and fear.
